subject: Urgent: Request to Accelerate small-scope feature for Harborline pilot
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Hart <julia.hart@harborline.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Request to Accelerate small-scope feature for Harborline pilot

Laura / Monica —

Quick context: Harborline (prospect -> pilot) just confirmed commercial terms in principle and wants to run a constrained pilot starting mid-July. Their primary blocker is a lightweight tenant-level export of inference logs and per-request metadata (redacted) for auditability. They’ve flagged this as a gating requirement for procurement.

What they need (minimal viable scope to unblock procurement):
- Per-tenant downloadable audit bundle (last 30 days) with redaction rules applied
- Simple CSV + JSON manifest format (see attached requested-scope-MVP.xlsx)
- Activation flag at tenant-level with an API route for exports only (no long-term retention change)

They’re willing to accept the following tradeoffs to get this in the pilot:
- Pilot limited to US region and 3 endpoints only
- Agreement to opt-in to a slightly higher per-token price for pilot period

Attachments: Harborline_SOW_v2.pdf (terms), requested-scope-MVP.xlsx (format + sample).

Ask: can Product commit to a scoped implementation for Q3 pilot? If not, what’s the smallest acceptable scope and timeline (ETA)? Procurement is asking for clear gating language by next Monday so we can include in the SOW.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Julia Hart <julia.hart@harborline.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Request to Accelerate small-scope feature for Harborline pilot

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. I skimmed the SOW and the requested sheet. A quick product read: the desired export (per-tenant bundle with basic redaction) is feasible but not currently on the roadmap as a first-class self-serve primitive. A few clarifying Qs before I commit a timeline: 

1) Redaction rules: are these strictly pattern-based (PII regex) or will they require semantic redaction (PII detection model)? Pattern-based is much faster to scope.
2) Export frequency/size: you mentioned 30 days. Do they expect a single bulk export endpoint or a paginated export job?
3) SLAs: do they need the export to be delivered synchronously or can it be generated as an async job with a callback URL?

Assuming pattern-based redaction and async job model limited to three endpoints in us-west-2, we could consider a scoped delivery as follows:
- Spike + design: 2 weeks
- Implementation (core export API + simple redaction pipeline): 4 weeks
- QA & rollout (canary to 1 tenant): 1 week
Total: ~7 weeks from sign-off. That would put us into late July / early August depending on resourcing.

Constraining notes: we’d want this behind a feature flag and not change retention semantics globally. Also need to confirm security review for export delivery channel (S3 vs direct download).

If you can confirm redaction approach + acceptance criteria, I’ll raise a small-scope ticket and try to align an engineer for the 2-week spike.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Platform | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Julia Hart <julia.hart@harborline.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Request to Accelerate small-scope feature for Harborline pilot

Laura — thanks for the quick assessment. Answers below to your questions and a proposed acceptance criteria set so we can be specific in procurement language: 

1) Redaction: pattern-based only for pilot (PII regex set supplied by Harborline). They explicitly said no semantic redaction for now to keep scope small.
2) Export model: async job that produces a single downloadable bundle (zip) with a JSON manifest + per-request JSON lines file + CSV summary. Max size expected ~2GB for 30 days (their traffic is modest).
3) Delivery: async job with signed S3 URL (30-day expiry) is acceptable.

Proposed acceptance criteria (pilot scope):
- Admin API to request export for tenant X for N days (default 30)
- Job status endpoint and single downloadable bundle (zip) with manifest + data files
- Pattern-based redaction applied server-side; redaction rules supplied via secure upload in the account portal
- Feature flag gated; enabled for Harborline tenant only in us-west-2
- Security review (redaction + S3 delivery) completed before first tenant activation

Commercial trade: Harborline agrees to sign SOW with a 6-week pilot at a 12% uplift on hosted pricing and provides a test tenant immediately upon DocuSign. Procurement wants these acceptance criteria in the SOW.

If Product can commit to the ~7-week timeline you sketched (2wk spike + 4wk build + 1wk QA), I will push to get DocuSign started and loop in Procurement. We can also do a smaller POC (single endpoint, 7-day window) faster if that helps.

Attaching a short SOW version in the thread (Harborline_SOW_v2.pdf).

Rafael

---
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Julia Hart <julia.hart@harborline.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Request to Accelerate small-scope feature for Harborline pilot

Thanks all — quick alignment from CS + Sales leadership side.

Ben and I discussed and we’re able to support a staged canary approach to reduce risk:
- Phase 0 (fast unblock, target 2 weeks): single-endpoint POC (7-day window), manual export produced by Ops using the same payload format. Procurement can accept this as interim language while Product works on the scoped feature.
- Phase 1 (targeted feature delivery): scoped export API behind a feature flag limited to Harborline tenant in us-west-2. Acceptance criteria per Rafael’s list. Goal: ship feature for pilot by end of July if Product can allocate 1 engineer full-time after spike.

Ben also confirmed flexibility on the commercial uplift (12% for pilot) if Product prioritizes the scoped ticket for the July window.

Laura — can you confirm if a 2-week spike plus a prioritized single-engineer delivery slot is plausible? If yes, I will ask Procurement to hold off on hard gating language until the POC is complete and add the Phase 1 commitment as a conditional item in the SOW.

Next steps: Rafael to share HubSpot deal link and updated SOW with conditional language; Laura to create spike ticket and scope.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
